events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: South Central Mountains; Quay County; Curry County; Roosevelt County; De Baca County; Chaves County Plains; Eastern Lincoln County; Southwest Chaves County
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Portions of east-central and southeast New Mexico,
including the following areas, in central New Mexico, Eastern
Lincoln County and South Central Mountains. In east central New
Mexico, Quay, Curry, Roosevelt, and De Baca Counties. In southeast
New Mexico, Chaves County Plains and Southwest Chaves County.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Rounds of showers and storms will continue through tonight.
Rainfall rates up to 2 inches per hour will have the potential to
produce rapid runoff, especially during the afternoon and evening
hours on Thursday. Soils are becoming increasingly saturated from
persistent rainfall over the past couple of days, further
elevating the risk of flash flooding. Rainfall amounts will
generally range from 1 to 2 inches, with isolated totals up to 3
inches.
- Rapid runoff and flash flooding will be most likely in complex
terrain, below recent burn scars, low-lying areas, urban areas,
normally dry arroyos, near rivers and streams, and in locations
where the ground is already saturated from recent heavy rainfall.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

* WHERE...Upper Florida Keys.

* WHEN...Through late tonight.

* IMPACTS...Minor saltwater flooding of low elevation streets
and lots is likely. Some storm drains will overflow, and some
seawalls and docks will be overtopped. Boaters can expect less
clearance under fixed bridges. Motorists should remember that
persistent puddles around the times of high tide are almost
certain to contain a mix of saltwater.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Eddy, NM
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
FFWMAF

The National Weather Service in Midland/Odessa has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Eddy County in southeastern New Mexico...

* Until 815 AM MDT.

* At 522 AM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Mesonet stations indicate that
between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen over the warned area.
Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Carlsbad, Loving, Carlsbad North, Avalon, Brantley Lake State Park,
Malaga, Seven Rivers Airport, Lake Avalon, Living Desert State
Park, Otis, Cavern City Air Terminal, Lakewood, Dayton, Lea County
Zip Franklin Memorial Airport, Loco Hills and Atoka.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Pima, AZ
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Small stream flooding caused by excessive rainfall
continues.

* WHERE...Central Pima County in southeastern Arizona, including
Cababi and Comobabi...

* WHEN...Until 600 AM MST.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas. Some
low-water crossings may become impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 419 AM MST, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain fell due to
thunderstorms earlier this morning. This will cause small stream
flooding. Between 0.5 and 1 inch of rain has fallen.
- Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall is
expected.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Cababi, Comobabi, Sil Nakya, Santa Rosa Ranch, San Luis - Sells
District and Rincon.
- This includes the following Flash Flood Prone Locations...
Sil Nakya Wash at Route 34.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.summary:
* WHAT...Minor flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Wilkes County in northwestern North Carolina...

* WHEN...Until 1015 AM EDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Overflowing poor drainage areas. Ponding of water in urban or other
areas is occurring or is imminent.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

advisory area. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have fallen.
- This includes the following streams and drainages...
Big Warrior Creek, Camp Branch, Cub Creek, Big Sandy Creek, Clear
Branch, Beaver Creek, Church Branch, Bussels Creek, Cane Creek,
Cove Creek, Bee Tree Branch, Big Bugaboo Creek and Basin Creek.
Additional rainfall amounts up to 1 inch are expected over the
area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
North Wilkesboro, Wilkesboro, Ronda, Traphill, Mc Grady, Boomer
and Wilbar.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
